channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: No TCU, ministro vota pela aprovação das contas de Lula em 2025, com ressalvas
item.description: TCU minister Benjamin Zymler voted to approve President Lula's 2025 accounts, with reservations. The vote highlighted an overestimation of R$60 billion in the 'other administered revenues' projection by the Federal Revenue in the 2024 budget law. Approval with reservations indicates acknowledgment of irregularities, but not invalidation of the accounts.

item.title: TSE cria grupo de trabalho para ampliar inclusão e fortalecer a centralidade do eleitor
item.description: The TSE has established a Working Group to enhance voter inclusion and centrality, focusing on women, Black people, Indigenous peoples, and persons with disabilities. The group will assess access barriers, map institutional and technological challenges, and propose actions to make Electoral Justice services more accessible and efficient.

item.title: Em evento do PT, Janones ensina apoiadores de Lula a enganar eleitores nas redes
item.description: A PT held a training session for Lula supporters teaching how to spread disinformation on social media, with Deputy André Janones arguing that truth is unnecessary as long as invented stories seem believable. He exemplified this by using edited photos of Bolsonaro and Collor to falsely suggest a potential ministerial appointment, claiming the word 'could' made it not a lie. The live YouTube broadcast revealed a deliberate strategy to deceive voters under the guise of 'telling one's version of the facts'.

item.title: Trump vira 'cabo eleitoral de Lula', mostra pesquisa Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll shows that Flávio Bolsonaro's association with Donald Trump is benefiting Lula, as independent voters link Flávio's alleged request for funding the 'Dark Horse' film to corruption suspicions. Furthermore, there is a perception that Flávio influenced Trump to designate PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations and to impose new tariffs on Brazilian products, reinforcing the Lula government's narrative that the senator is acting against national interests.

item.title: Eleitor considera Lula mais patriota que Flávio Bolsonaro, aponta pesquisa Genial/Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 47% of voters view Lula as more patriotic than Flávio Bolsonaro, compared to 37% for the senator. This perception is linked to the U.S. threat of tariffs on Brazilian exports, which voters associate with the Bolsonaro family’s efforts to gain Trump’s support for the 2026 election. Additionally, 46% believe the U.S. tariffs are a retaliation against Brazil’s Pix payment system, reinforcing the view that Lula better defends national interests.

item.title: Michelle diz que vai apoiar campanha de Flávio, mas só no “momento certo”
item.description: Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro announced she will support Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, but only 'at the right moment,' as her current priority is caring for her husband, Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest until the end of June. She also said her potential Senate candidacy depends on his health improvement. The statement comes amid family tensions, following earlier speculation that Michelle might replace Flávio on the presidential ticket.

item.title: Justiça suspende expulsão de Rebelo do DC e pede reintegração, após desavença por candidatura de Barbosa
item.description: The Federal District Court suspended the expulsion of Aldo Rebelo from the Christian Democracy (DC) party and ordered his reinstatement, ruling that the expulsion violated the party's internal disciplinary due process. The court also imposed a fine of R$ 50,000 for non-compliance. Rebelo is seeking to regain his presidential pre-candidacy, which was withdrawn in favor of Joaquim Barbosa following an internal party dispute.

item.title: Confira a pauta de julgamentos do TSE desta quinta-feira (11/6)
item.description: The TSE will rule on five cases from the 2024 Municipal Elections, including an appeal against the TRE-BA’s dismissal of an AIJE concerning alleged gender quota fraud in the candidacy of Luana Araújo de Queiroz (Avante) for councilwoman in Valente (BA). Other highlights include campaign finance review for the elected mayor of Imperatriz (MA) and AI-generated videos aimed at influencing voters in Campo Bom (RS).

item.title: Rogerio Marinho critica política fiscal e alerta para dívida pública
item.description: Senator Rogerio Marinho (PL-RN) criticized the federal government's fiscal policy, stating that rising public spending and taxation — including over 12 percentage points of additional tax burden and nearly R$300 billion in new taxes — are driving Brazil's public debt to 84% of GDP, up from 71%. He warned this will leave a 'toxic inheritance' of over R$2 trillion in debt for future generations, citing the decline in state-owned enterprises, particularly Correios, which went from a surplus under Bolsonaro to requiring billions in loans due to political mismanagement.

item.title: Como os brasileiros enxergam as ações de Trump sobre tarifas e Pix, segundo pesquisa
item.description: A Quaest survey shows 46% of Brazilians agree with Lula that new U.S. tariffs are a retaliation against Pix, while 36% support Flávio Bolsonaro’s view that tariffs respond to Lula’s criticism of the U.S. The USTR document cites Pix as a justification for 25% tariffs, claiming Brazil’s central bank unfairly favors Pix over U.S. payment services by mandating free access and prominent placement in bank apps.

item.title: Aniversariante do dia, Ancelotti passa por corredor polonês durante treino da seleção brasileira
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti celebrated his 67th birthday during a Brazil national team training session, where players honored him with the 'Polish corridor'. The CBF praised his global football legacy, noting his unprecedented success across five European leagues and five Champions League titles, and expressed hope he will lead Brazil to a historic sixth World Cup in 2026.

item.title: Decisivo, eleitor ‘independente’ passa a dar vantagem confortável a Lula contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The independent electorate, the largest segment in the Genial/Quaest poll, has shifted to give Lula a comfortable lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, with 37% to 24%, reversing a prior trend. Lula also improved his approval among independents, cutting his net negative from 26 to just 6 points, while Flávio Bolsonaro declined even in first-round support, from 18% to 14%. Independents constitute 32% of the sample and are pivotal to the 2026 electoral dynamics.

item.title: Justiça cancela expulsão e manda DC reintegrar Aldo Rebelo
item.description: The Federal District Court suspended the expulsion of Aldo Rebelo from the Christian Democracy party (DC), ordering his reinstatement within 72 hours under threat of a fine. The ruling cited the lack of a proper disciplinary process, which violated Rebelo’s right to defense and contradiction, as well as the party’s statute. While Rebelo seeks to maintain his presidential pre-candidacy, the DC plans to launch former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa as its candidate.

item.title: Censura à Atlas: os dois impasses cruciais sobre pesquisas eleitorais que o TSE terá de resolver
item.description: The TSE postponed the referendum on the injunction that censored AtlasIntel's poll about Flávio Bolsonaro, delaying the establishment of crucial guidelines for electoral polls. Two central impasses remain: whether pollsters can include multimedia content (audio/video) in surveys and how to address claims of decontextualization or deepfakes. The Court tends to ban such materials, deeming them unnecessary and risky for electoral integrity.

item.title: Ministros do STF e costura de bastidor mudaram tendência do TSE sobre ação de Flávio contra pesquisa
item.description: The preliminary ruling by TSE Minister Kassio Nunes Marques suspending the Atlas poll showing Flávio Bolsonaro in decline initially had majority support in the plenary, but was reversed after press criticism and interventions from STF ministers, who warned of the TSE being undermined if the decision stood. TSE ministers then sought dialogue with polling institutes and experts to establish objective criteria for evaluating poll neutrality, avoiding subjective judgments by individual judges. Despite the conflict, Nunes Marques was viewed positively for demonstrating openness to dialogue with opposing views.

item.title: Glauber Braga retoma mandato 6 meses após suspensão e amplia ataques aos Bolsonaros
item.description: Deputy Glauber Braga resumed his congressional mandate after a six-month suspension for assaulting an MBL member. He announced plans to introduce legislation holding Senators Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro financially accountable for their actions with the Trump administration, which he labeled as 'conspiratorial' against Brazil’s interests. Braga also linked the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations to Bolsonaro brothers’ support and criticized new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: O tratamento que salvou voz de Lula ainda não chega a todos os brasileiros
item.description: President Lula undergoes radiotherapy again after removal of a basal cell carcinoma, highlighting his privileged access to advanced technologies like IMRT, which are not widely available in the SUS. Despite being essential in about 60% of cancer cases and responsible for 40% of cures, radiotherapy accounts for only 5% of oncology spending in Brazil, suffering from chronic underfunding and outdated payment tables. The disparity between the high-quality treatment received by the president and the reality for most Brazilians underscores inequality in access to oncological healthcare in the country.

item.title: TSE adia decisão sobre suspensão de pesquisa: entenda o que está sendo julgado e como sondagens são feitas
item.description: The TSE postponed its ruling on the suspension of an AtlasIntel poll showing declining voter intention for Flávio Bolsonaro following leaked audio related to the Master case. TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques had previously ordered the poll’s suspension individually, citing inducement of responses, with the tribunal’s current vote at 1-0 in favor of suspension. Experts note that electoral polls rely on statistical sampling but can be skewed by question wording and context, prompting ongoing debate about their accuracy and limitations.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Flávio cai… de novo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) recorded another decline in voting intentions according to the Genial Quaest poll released Wednesday. The Meio-Dia em Brasília program also covered the suspension of the TSE ruling on the AtlasIntel poll and the PEC reducing the age of criminal responsibility.

item.title: Genial/Quest: Lula avança entre independentes e abre vantagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula leads with 39% in the first round and 44% in a potential runoff, expanding his advantage over Flávio Bolsonaro, particularly among independent voters, where he rose from 29% to 37% while the senator fell from 31% to 24%. Government approval rose to 47%, technically tying disapproval, driven by policies like Desenrola and IR exemptions, while Flávio faces backlash over film financing allegations and Banco Master suspicions.

item.title: Quaest: 46% concordam com Lula e dizem que tarifas de Trump são retaliação ao PIX
item.description: The Quaest poll shows 46% of respondents agree with President Lula that new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products are retaliation against the PIX system, while 36% support Flávio Bolsonaro’s view that the tariffs are a reaction to Lula’s criticisms of the United States. 10% reject both explanations, and 8% did not know or did not respond. The survey was conducted between June 5 and 8, 2026, with 2,004 respondents aged 16 or older, a margin of error of 2 percentage points, and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Quaest: Entre eleitores independentes, Lula passa Flávio Bolsonaro e abre 13 pontos de vantagem no 2º turno
item.description: Lula opened a 13-point lead over Flávio Bolsonaro among independent voters in the June Quaest poll, rising from 29% to 37% while Flávio fell from 31% to 24%. In the overall scenario, Lula leads with 44% against Flávio's 38%, breaking the May technical tie. The shift occurred mainly among voters who do not identify with any ideological camp, representing a third of the electorate.

item.title: Relator mantém autonomia financeira do BC sem mudanças pedidas pelo governo
item.description: Senator Plínio Valério maintained his report on the Central Bank's financial autonomy without incorporating the government base's demands, which sought to subject the BC to spending and personnel caps set by the CMN. He stated he did not accept the suggestions and expects a tight vote in the CCJ, with possible government obstruction. The proposal, which would allow the BC to manage its own budget using asset-generated revenues, is supported by financial analysts and BC President Gabriel Galípolo as key to ensuring operational continuity, including for initiatives like Pix.

item.title: Toffoli não resiste a tutelar o eleitor
item.description: Minister Dias Toffoli, upon returning to the TSE as an effective member, delivered a speech defending voter autonomy, but later advocated for voter tutelage when commenting on the suspension of the AtlasIntel poll, revealing a contradiction in his stance.

item.title: Flávio é rejeitado por 56% e Lula por 53%, diz Quaest
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula at 39% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 38% in first-round voting intentions, with Lula leading in all second-round scenarios. Both candidates face high rejection: Lula rejected by 53%, Flávio by 56%, following a scandal involving a request for funds to produce a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Lula's government approval stands at 47% versus 48% disapproval, with ratings split between positive (34%), regular (26%) and negative (38%).

item.title: Justiça suspende expulsão de Aldo Rebelo da DC e determina que ele seja reintegrado ao partido
item.description: The Federal District Court suspended the summary expulsion of Aldo Rebelo from the Christian Democracy (DC) party for violating due process, ordering his reinstatement within 72 hours under a R$ 50,000 fine. The decision followed Rebelo's public criticism of the party's move to replace him as presidential pre-candidate with former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa and his allegations against party president João Caldas. Rebelo aims to compel a party convention to decide the DC's presidential candidate between himself and Barbosa.

item.title: Zanin e Dino divergem de Moraes e votam para atender pedido de Garotinho
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court voted two to one to overturn a decision that removed posts by former governor Anthony Garotinho, granting his appeal. While rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes maintained his opposing vote, ministers Cristiano Zanin and Flávio Dino dissented, arguing the lower court failed to assess the truthfulness of the content or the limits of press freedom. Minister Cármen Lúcia requested a view, leaving the outcome pending.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Para 47%, Flávio influenciou decisão dos EUA de designar PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll shows that 47% of Brazilians believe Senator Flávio Bolsonaro influenced the U.S. decision to designate PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, while 37% disagree and 16% are unsure. While 60% support classifying the groups as terrorists by the Brazilian government, opinions on the U.S. move are evenly split (45% in favor, 45% opposed), with 53% expecting negative impacts on Brazilian businesses and banks.

item.title: Marinho diz em Genebra que IA deve libertar trabalhador
item.description: Labor and Employment Minister Luiz Marinho advocated at the ILO in Geneva that AI-driven productivity gains should be shared with workers through fair wages, technology access, and reduced working hours. He stressed that technological advancement is not inevitable and depends on political choices, institutional strength, and social dialogue, aligning with a proposed constitutional amendment to cut the workweek to 40 hours and eliminate the 6x1 schedule.

item.title: Caso Master, Pix e tarifaço: pesquisa capta como a população avalia a atuação de Flávio e Lula no último bimestre
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula leading in the first round with stability since May, while Flávio Bolsonaro drops from 33% to 29% due to news about his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro and the Trump administration. Lula leads in all tested second-round scenarios. The survey captures voter reactions to recent crises, scandals, tensions, and economic measures.

item.title: TSE se mete em confusão com censura pedida por Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The TSE postponed a decision on banning an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll showing voter rejection of Flávio Bolsonaro due to his ties with Daniel Vorcaro, jailed for financial fraud. Judge Kassio Nunes Marques supported the PL and Bolsonaro’s censorship request, claiming non-neutral questions, but the plenary vote was halted by a procedural maneuver. The move clashes with Article 220 of the Constitution, which bans political, ideological, or artistic censorship.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: Maioria acha que Flávio sabia de corrupção e errou ao pedir dinheiro a Vorcaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 62% of Brazilians believe Senator Flávio Bolsonaro knew Daniel Vorcaro was involved in corruption and erred by asking him for money to fund the film 'Dark Horse'. Among Bolsonaro supporters, opinions are split: 42% think he made a mistake, 42% do not. A majority (58%) suspect illegal involvement, and 50% of voters say they would no longer vote for him, making this a significant negative factor for his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy.

item.title: Quaest mostra oscilação positiva na aprovação do governo Lula
item.description: The Quaest/Genial poll shows President Lula's approval rating rose to 47%, while disapproval stands at 48%, resulting in a technical tie within the two-point margin of error. Although disapproval remains slightly higher, this marks one of Lula’s best approval ratings in recent years, up from 40% in May 2025 and 43% in April 2026. The survey interviewed 2,004 people across 120 Brazilian municipalities from June 5–8 and was registered with the TSE under code BR-07661/2026.

item.title: Quaest: 60% dizem que PCC e CV devem ser considerados organizações terroristas pelo governo brasileiro
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 60% of respondents agree that the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) should be designated as terrorist organizations by the Brazilian government, while 29% disagree and 11% are unsure. Furthermore, 47% believe Flávio Bolsonaro influenced the U.S. decision to label these groups as terrorist, compared to 37% who say he had no involvement.

item.title: Flávio perde votos entre independentes após mensagens com Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) lost support among independent voters, with his voting intentions dropping from 31% to 24% in the presidential race against Lula (PT), according to the Genial/Quaest poll. The sharpest decline followed the release of messages between Flávio and businessman Vorcaro, which caused political damage. These voters shifted to Lula, reflecting the negative impact of the controversy on Flávio’s perceived reliability.

item.title: Genial/Quaest mostra melhora na avaliação do governo Lula e impacto negativo de Master e tarifas sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll showed a slight recovery in the government’s approval and an increase in Lula’s voting intention, both spontaneous and stimulated. Positive developments, including the income tax exemption, contributed to the improvement, with the share of people reporting income growth rising from 25% to 32%, especially among those earning up to two minimum wages.

item.title: TSE: o Judiciário realmente descobriu o prazer de mandar
item.description: The article criticizes judicial activism in Brazil, arguing that the judiciary has assumed legislative functions when Congress fails or makes unpopular decisions, representing a deviation from the separation of powers and a threat to democracy. It suggests this tendency, once started, is difficult to reverse.

item.title: Lula venceria qualquer adversário em segundo turno, mostra Quaest
item.description: President Lula leads all second-round scenarios against right-wing and far-right opponents, with advantages ranging from 6 to 14 percentage points. In the Quaest poll, he received between 44% and 45% of voting intentions, while his opponents ranged from 31% to 38%. The survey interviewed 2,004 people between June 5 and 8, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Governo Lula é desaprovado por 48% e aprovado por 47%, diz Quaest
item.description: The June 2026 Quaest poll shows President Lula’s government with 48% disapproval and 47% approval, with 38% rating his administration negatively and 34% positively. Lula leads first-round voting intentions at 39%, and would defeat Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff by 44% to 38%, widening his lead from the technical tie in May. The survey was conducted after reports emerged that Flávio Bolsonaro solicited funds for a film about Jair Bolsonaro’s trajectory.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se distancia de Lula no 2º turno após revelação de relações com Vorcaro, mostra Quaest
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) trails Lula (PT) by six points in a potential runoff, according to a Quaest/Genial Investimentos poll released on June 10, 2026. The decline follows revelations of his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master, including requests for funding the film 'Dark Horse', which 65% of respondents deemed a mistake. In the first-round scenario, Flávio is ten points behind Lula, who leads in all tested matchups.

item.title: Quaest também capta queda de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll showed a decline in Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) standing against Lula (PT) following the leak of messages he sent to banker Daniel Vorcaro. This downward trend had already been signaled by earlier polls such as Datafolha and Nexus. The survey underscores the negative impact of the scandal on Bolsonaro's candidacy.

item.title: Quaest: 47% concordam que Flávio pediu a Trump tarifaço contra o Brasil
item.description: A Quaest poll reveals that 47% of respondents agree with Lula’s claim that Flávio Bolsonaro requested the new U.S. tariffs on Brazil, while 35% side with Flávio, who says he asked Trump to avoid imposing new tariffs. Half of the interviewees were aware of the May meeting between Flávio and Trump. The survey, conducted June 5–8, 2026, interviewed 2,004 people aged 16+ with a 2-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Desenrola 2 beneficiou apenas 10% da população, de acordo com pesquisa Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll found that the Desenrola 2 program directly benefited only 10% of Brazil's population, according to an exclusive report. The Lula government had bet on the program as a strategy to boost its popularity, but its impact has been limited so far.

item.title: Lula tem 44% contra 38% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Quaest
item.description: A June 2026 Quaest poll shows Lula leading with 44% against Flávio Bolsonaro’s 38% in a hypothetical second-round scenario, widening his lead after a technical tie in May. Lula also leads in all other second-round matchups tested (against Zema, Caiado, and Renan Santos) and is ahead in the first round with 39% versus Flávio’s 29%. Most respondents (55%) are aware of the conversations between Flávio and Daniel Vorcaro regarding film financing, and 65% believe the senator erred in maintaining contact.

item.title: Quaest: 48% desaprovam e 47% aprovam governo Lula
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula's government approval at 47% and disapproval at 48%, a technical tie with a one-point margin. This marks significant improvement from April, when the gap was nine points. Among independent voters, crucial for the election, approval rose from 32% to 41% and disapproval fell from 58% to 47%.

item.title: Alvaro Dias lidera disputa ao Senado no PR, diz pesquisa
item.description: Alvaro Dias (MDB) leads the Senate race in Paraná with 37.7% of voting intentions, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey released on June 10, 2026. Deltan Dallagnol (Novo), Gleisi Hoffmann (PT), Filipe Barros (PL), and Alexandre Curi (Republicanos) follow in a technical tie within the 2.6-point margin of error. The study, registered with the TSE as PR-06978/2026, surveyed 1,500 people across 56 municipalities from June 7–9 and was funded by the Liberal Party.

item.title: Michelle sugere que eleitores sejam mesários e fiscais do PL
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro urged supporters to become poll workers and monitors for the PL in the 2026 elections, stressing the need for greater female participation in electoral oversight. The 'Operation V2 – Watch and Vote' campaign launched with national radio and TV ads until June 20 and will continue on social media until July 20. She emphasized that the initiative increases transparency, enables vote monitoring, and provides legal benefits, encouraging women to register with the TRE or volunteer for the party.

item.title: A pesquisa eleitoral suspensa por Nunes Marques a pedido de Flávio - O Assunto #1.736
item.description: TSE Minister Nunes Marques monocratically suspended an Atlas Intel poll showing declining support for Flávio Bolsonaro after revelations that he solicited funds from Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse'. The ruling cited alleged 'methodological contamination' due to questions about the Banco Master scandal, despite Atlas Intel stating the questions were added post-electoral questionnaire and did not affect results. The TSE plenary began voting to uphold or overturn the injunction, as experts debate the unprecedented nature of the decision and the role of polls in informing voters.

item.title: Boulos explica em vídeo como será a rede “Porta-Vozes do Lula”
item.description: Minister Guilherme Boulos (Psol-SP) explained the functioning of the 'Porta-Vozes do Lula' platform, created by the PT to coordinate the activity of militants and influencers on social media during the pre-campaign for Lula's re-election. The initiative aims to counter the right's superiority in digital narrative organization by providing daily posting topics via WhatsApp, seeking to build discursive unity among supporters and prevent the left from remaining on the defensive.

item.title: Em meio à nova ameaça tarifária de Trump, Lula participa de reunião com empresários nesta quarta
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the meeting of the Council for Sustainable Economic and Social Development (Conselhão) amid new U.S. tariff threats targeting Brazilian goods, with proposed rates up to 37,5%. The 10 a.m. session at Itamaraty will focus on national sovereignty, multilateralism, and international agenda, including presentations of the council’s work and a guide on combating femicide. In the afternoon, Vice President Geraldo Alckmin will lead a panel on economic, social, and sustainable development pathways.
